name: How to Plan and Build a Bathroom Addition From Start to Finish

step.name: Step 1: Complete an initial feasibility walk and measure your existing structural spans.
step.text: Your contractor inspects the floor joists, main water supply, existing vent stacks, and electrical panel capacity to confirm the home can feed new fixtures without heavy service upgrades. You will want to have rough room dimensions and a wishlist of plumbing fixtures ready for this review.

step.name: Step 2: Draft measured floor plans and submit applications for building, plumbing, and electrical permits.
step.text: Detailed drawings map out fixture clearances, wall framing, dedicated GFCI electrical circuits, and mandatory mechanical ventilation paths to your local building department. Construction should stay on hold until jurisdictional approval is officially in hand.

step.name: Step 3: Frame custom walls and complete rough plumbing, electrical, and HVAC runs.
step.text: Carpenters build out the stud walls while trade specialists rough in supply lines, drain-waste-vent pipes, exhaust ducting, and wiring. This step wraps up only when local municipal inspectors review and sign off on all open-wall rough inspections.

step.name: Step 4: Install backer board, apply continuous waterproofing, and conduct shower flood testing.
step.text: Crews hang cement board and apply fluid or sheet waterproofing membranes across wet zones before laying a single piece of tile. Testing the shower pan with standing water confirms the assembly is completely watertight prior to closing up finishes.

step.name: Step 5: Lay tile, hang and finish drywall, and paint interior surfaces.
step.text: Tile specialists set floor and wall tiles, grout joints, and seal porous stone, while drywall pros tape, mud, sand, and prime adjacent drywall. Done looks like smooth walls, flat tile planes, and crisp transition trim across every doorway.

step.name: Step 6: Set finish fixtures, install custom trim, and pass final municipal inspections.
step.text: The crew sets the vanity, secures the toilet, trims out faucets, hangs lighting, and applies finish baseboards and door casings. A final inspection from your local building official closes the permit cleanly. When you are ready to evaluate fixture layouts or floor framing for a bathroom addition in the Denver metro area, call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
